text.audienceNote: VP and C-suite clicks reached 6 in September, the most this year, and real estate, finance and strategy leaders clicked 15 times after none in August. Real estate, facilities and finance titles were 9% of impressions, so there is room to grow reach with those leaders.
text.searchTermsNote: Healthcare search terms are broad ("healthcare solution providers," "healthcare software companies"). Adding negative keywords for software and practice-startup searches would focus spend on real estate intent.
text.budgetNote: Conferences ($52K) and videography ($20K) are budgeted in November and December, so year-end utilization depends on those landing.
text.fatigueNote: No sign of fatigue: the long-running Outlook and Boldt Difference ads held or improved their click-through rates. Refresh on frequency (more than about 4 impressions per person per month) rather than on a calendar.
bestPractices: Lead with a point of view on cost and risk
Cost-certainty statements ("The lowest number rarely survives delivery.") average 1.85% click-through vs 1.05% for brand promises and 0.54% for direct asks.
Keep Boldt out of the headline
Headlines that name Boldt average 0.86% vs 1.52% without; the logo and page name already carry the brand.
Specific, complete-sentence headlines average 1.59% vs 1.07% for 6 words or fewer, and cost about a third as much per conversion.
Earn the click before asking for a meeting
"Schedule a meeting" and "Contact our experts" average 0.54% at $9.96 per click. Save direct asks for retargeting.
Match every high-click ad with a converting page
Cost-certainty ads drew 1,023 clicks and no conversions; fix the landing page before adding budget.
Use document ads for retargeting only
Document lead gen costs $1,250 per conversion vs $603 for image ads, with a 0.25% click-through rate.
Financing and ownership headlines average 0.71% at $7.33 per click. State the outcome (for example, capital freed or rent avoided) rather than the product name.
Test in pairs, judge at 10,000 impressions
Run 2 to 3 headlines per theme and wait for 10,000 impressions each before calling a winner.

exec.headline: September SQLs rebounded to 4 after none in August, and year-to-date SQLs are 57% ahead of 2025. MQLs matched September 2025 at 22 on lower spend, bringing cost per MQL down to $404 from $534 in August.

sections.title: Results
sections.body: Healthcare marketing produced 22 new MQLs in September, the same as September 2025 and down from 27 in August, against a monthly goal of 37. Year to date, MQLs total 233, which is 70% of the conservative goal and 16% below the same months of 2025. SQLs are the strongest signal: 4 in September and 33 for the year versus 21 in 2025, and MQL-to-SQL conversion is 14.2% compared with 6.8% last year.

sections.title: What went well
bullets: Lower cost per lead. Healthcare marketing spend was $8,881 in September, the lowest month this year, and cost per MQL fell to $404 from $534 in August.
LinkedIn got more efficient as spend came down: cost per click fell to $4.15 from $7.11, and LinkedIn conversions rose to 11 from 4.
Google search kept bringing low-cost traffic, with healthcare campaigns at a 7% to 10.5% click-through rate and $0.19 to $0.78 per click.

Our LinkedIn ads are reaching decision makers: 81% of September impressions with a job title reached directors and above, VP and C-suite clicks reached 6 (the most this year), and real estate, finance and strategy leaders clicked 15 times, up from none in August.
Willis-Knighton Health System visited the site after seeing our LinkedIn ads and became an MQL on September 30.

sections.title: Where we are focused
bullets: MQL volume trails last year: 233 from January through September versus 277 in 2025, down 16%. That holds cost per MQL at $459 for the year versus $390 in 2025.
Growing LinkedIn reach among real estate, facilities and finance leaders, who were 9% of September impressions, to build on this month's gains in executive clicks.
Healthcare website sessions fell 19% to 1,379, mostly because LinkedIn traffic halved (106 sessions vs 221 in August) as LinkedIn spend came down.

sections.title: Budget
sections.body: Healthcare and shared marketing spend is $129K through September, 70% of the budget to date. September came in at $11.4K against $20.3K budgeted, and LinkedIn healthcare spent $2,115 of its $5,833 line. Conferences ($52K) and videography ($20K) are scheduled for November and December.

nextMonth: Shift more LinkedIn budget toward real estate, facilities, finance and strategy leaders to build on September's gains.
Relaunch the cost-certainty landing page with a shorter form and a clearer next step.
Put the unused LinkedIn budget behind new cost-certainty image ads and the Financial Options launch.
Tighten Google search terms to real estate intent.
